title: Who played at the Okeh ball and the party afterward
summary: She lists performers present, says it lasted until two in the morning with more white than Black guests, and why she could not enjoy it.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands

blocks.x: They're all right, they're all right. That's no problem. Now, do you remember -- did Joe Oliver, was he on the program that night?
And Richard Jordan (PHONETIC) to play the trombone.
Uh-huh. And everybody, every piano player you could mention was there. There was a gang of piano players. It lasted until 2:00 o'clock.
Until 2:00 o'clock. What time did it start?
And when we left from there -- it started early.
(Unintelligible) some cabaret and I was quite young to go in the cabaret. But someplace where they could get something to drink. And so --
Well, that was 1926. That was during the Prohibition. You mean nobody could have anything to drink during that big night there?

Now who came to that celebration?
It was ______ thousand, a hundred thousand ______ people were there.
All kinds. It was more white than it was colored.
But we sure did have a nice time. I didn't know how to enjoy myself then. But Lord above, if it had been now, I would really know how to enjoy myself now.
